title: Typing, and then typing at the front
request:
two characters typed in order, then a third inserted after `root`

./your_program.sh rga
insert r1 root a1 h
insert r1 a1 a2 i
text r1
insert r1 root a3 o
text r1
note: `a3` and `a1` were both inserted after `root`, so they are siblings, and the larger id goes first. That single rule is what makes two replicas that never spoke agree on the order of characters they typed at the same spot.

title: A delete leaves something behind
request:
the second character is deleted, then something is inserted after it

./your_program.sh rga
insert r1 root a1 h
insert r1 a1 a2 i
delete r1 a2
text r1
insert r1 a2 a3 o
text r1
note: The deleted element has to stay in the structure with a flag on it. A replica that erases it cannot place `a3` at all when this arrives from elsewhere, and the two replicas have diverged over a character nobody can see.
